heroHeadline: Gang Suppression Force Begins Replacing Police in Kenscoff as Civilian Mediator's Hostage Release Fuels Accountability Crisis
heroSubtitle: Viv Ansanm coalition gunmen stormed Kenscoff on the night of August 23, 2026, torching roughly 25 homes and executing dozens inside a church sheltering earlier IDPs; the UN confirmed August 26 that the toll had risen to at least 47 killed, including 5+ children, with more than 50 people kidnapped — one of Haiti's largest mass-kidnapping incidents in recent years. The UN Security Council convened an emergency session August 28, where Special Representative Carlos Ruiz Massieu cited 1,408 people killed and 656 injured April–June alone and urged faster activation of Haiti's specialized judicial units; members pressed for the Gang Suppression Force's (GSF) acceleration toward its full 5,500-person mandate, with Chad and Mongolia having signed troop agreements. Community mediator Luckson Jean entered gang territory on August 28 and, with UNICEF support, secured the release of 13 hostages — six children and seven women — without ransom, intensifying scrutiny of the National Police response as PNH Director Vladimir Paraison's internal investigation into possible complicity or negligence remained unresolved; more than 40 hostages remained in gang custody. Per the joint PNH/AFH/GSF plan agreed after the massacre, the Gang Suppression Force began taking over PNH security positions in Kenscoff on September 1, freeing national police to reinforce the town while the GSF — still only ~1,000-strong against its 5,500-person ceiling — expands its own footprint elsewhere in Port-au-Prince, with its initial UN authorization set to expire September 30, 2026.
